summary.business: The Supreme Industries Limited manufactures a wide range of plastic products including uPVC/CPVC/HDPE/PVC piping systems, bath fittings and sanitaryware, roto-moulded tanks, moulded furniture, industrial components and material-handling products, flexible packaging and protective packaging films, composite LPG cylinders, and fabricated uPVC Windows & Doors. It serves the construction, packaging (FMCG/pharma/chemicals), automotive, furniture, consumer goods, and agriculture & irrigation industries across India and exports to 55 countries.

currentContext.strengths: Pan-India geographical spread of 35 manufacturing facilities across 13 States supporting efficient, economical customer servicing|Extensive distribution network — 7045 active Channel Partners as on 31 March 2026 (up from 5658 a year earlier), 32 Depots and 9 Fabrication facilities|Brand investment of ₹98 crore on brand awareness and influencer engagement, plus strong digital presence (Supreme Pipes Facebook page crossed 10 lakh followers; Corporate LinkedIn crossed 1 lakh followers)|Export reach to 55 countries with continuing efforts to widen geographic coverage|Active anti-counterfeiting vigilance program to protect brand integrity, particularly in the Pipe segment
currentContext.strategies: Broaden the pallet product range toward advanced, technology-driven storage and transportation solutions compatible with robotic and automatic storage systems.|Recover and regain lost market share in the export pallets segment by partnering with reliable suppliers to secure an uninterrupted raw-material supply chain.|Strengthen relationships with regular FMCG/Pharma customers for customized roto-moulded pallets through tailored service offerings.|Consolidate presence in eastern and southern coastal regions for Fisheries crates while targeting expansion of volume and market share in the western region.|Broaden customer coverage into previously unrepresented regions by increasing sales personnel and strengthening the channel network.|Composite LPG Cylinder division moving up the value chain into Compressed Biogas (CBG) cylinders, CNG cascades, and pressure-vessel/light-weighting technology via an investment in a start-up venture.|Performance Films Division to expand footprint across Middle East, EU, South America, Africa and Southeast Asia, with technical focus on high-barrier Polyamide & EVOH segments and vertical-based tailored offerings.|Protective Packaging Division pursuing continuous capacity expansion and technology upgradation across plants (Malanpur, Jadcherla, Hosur, Kharagpur, Urse) plus a planned greenfield facility in the Western region.|Cross Laminated Film segment targeting product/geographic diversification (first U.S. customer secured, positive response from Latin America) and expects newly signed FTAs to improve export price competitiveness.
currentContext.expansion: Protective Packaging Division carried out capacity expansion and technology upgradation across multiple plants during the year — an additional Capcell press at Malanpur; an upgraded XLPE line and a new high-productivity NBR line at Jadcherla; a new PU Foam Moulding plant at Hosur (a model the Company plans to replicate at other locations); two additional Capcell presses at Kharagpur; and a new EPE line at Urse. Further planned initiatives include relocating/upgrading an EPE line from Urse to Jadcherla, technical overhauling of EPE machines and installation of a new Calendar Roll at Hosur, overhauling of a Toshiba machine and installation of a Calendar Roll at Malanpur, and an XLPE line under evaluation at Kharagpur. The Division has completed land acquisition for a proposed greenfield manufacturing facility in the Western region close to a port, evaluating multiple product lines (PU Sheets, PU Moulding, XLPE, NBR, IXPE, Capcell, Litecell, PP Moulding) to serve export markets and West-zone customers. Separately, the Cross Laminated Film segment plans to launch a 'Cross Plastics' product in Q2 of the current year, subject to further refinement and successful customer trials. The Company funded large capital expenditure for capacity expansion — including the acquisition of 3 undertakings from the Wavin group on a slump-purchase basis — while remaining debt-free with a net cash surplus of ₹648.45 crores as on 31 March 2026, and continues to explore organic and inorganic growth avenues.

risks.note: Shifts in US tariff policies may disrupt global trade flows and impact export competitiveness; mitigated by a diversified procurement strategy (including sourcing from China) and the fact that about 98% of Company sales are domestic.

risks.risk: Geopolitical instability affecting supply chains and energy costs
risks.note: Persistent conflicts and regional tensions affect supply chains and energy costs; mitigated through a multi-vendor sourcing strategy for raw materials and maintaining strategic safety stocks of critical raw materials.

risks.risk: Global economic slowdown reducing infrastructure spending
risks.note: Slower growth in major economies may lead to reduced infrastructure spending; the Company focuses on domestic high-growth sectors such as urban infrastructure, agriculture and water management (including participation in various Government initiatives) to offset global headwinds.

As an importer of key raw materials, currency volatility impacts margins; managed through a consistent hedging policy using forward contracts and natural hedging (to some extent). Being debt-free, the Company has no currency/interest-rate risk from long-term or short-term foreign currency loans.

Delays in large-scale capex projects can lead to cost overruns; mitigated via cost-benefit analysis and stipulated timelines before beginning any capex project, with periodic progress tracking against budget by the Project Management team.

Cybersecurity, technology and operational risks are integral to the Company's enterprise risk management framework; mitigated through layered network security controls, AI-enabled threat detection, periodic vulnerability assessments, security audits and control reviews, plus business continuity and disaster recovery frameworks.
Risk of product failure is mitigated by subjecting every batch to stringent pressure and stress testing according to international standards (BIS/ISO).
The Company rigorously defends its trademarks, designs and patents, with its legal team proactively monitoring the market for infringements to protect market share and premium brand positioning.

one-line thesis: Supreme Industries delivered 12% volume growth in FY26 despite a 9% industry contraction, driven by market share gains and a ~INR 70-80 Cr Q4 inventory gain from PVC price spikes. Guidance for FY27 targets 12-13% overall volume growth (15-17% in piping) with margins stabilizing at 14-14.5%, though immediate Q1 faces margin pressure from falling resin prices.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 11,218 Cr (+7% YoY); EBITDA: INR 1,654 Cr (+7% YoY), Margin ~14.7%; PAT: INR 954 Cr (-1% YoY, impacted by tax/one-offs vs INR 961 Cr prior); Order Book: Not disclosed (Make-to-Stock model); Net Debt: Zero. One-offs: Q4 includes ~INR 70-80 Cr inventory gain due to March PVC price spike; Full-year labor provision adjusted to INR 14.4 Cr (down from Q3 estimate of INR 15.4 Cr).
guidance: FY27 Volume Growth: 12-13% overall, 15-17% for Piping segment; EBITDA Margin: 14.0-14.5%; Order Inflow: Agri demand picked up in April post-price correction; Capex: INR 1,000 Cr committed for FY27.
order book & pipeline: N/A (Company operates on make-to-stock with extensive distributor network; no specific project order book disclosed).
segment / subsidiary detail: Piping: +14% vol, +11% value (CPVC +38% vol); Industrial: -1% vol, -3% value; Packaging: +5% vol, +3% value; Consumer: +4% vol, -1% value. Value-added products grew 15% to INR 4,677 Cr.
growth verticals / optionality: Windows & Doors unit (Kanpur) started March '26, targeting INR 250 Cr annual revenue at full capacity with higher margins; Gas piping (electro-fusion fittings) expansion; Export target scaling from $5 Mn to $50 Mn; New packaging facility planned near JNPT.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margins supported by INR 70-80 Cr Q4 inventory gain; FY27 guidance 14-14.5% assumes normalized raw material costs. Current PVC prices dropped INR 34/kg in April, creating potential inventory loss headwinds for Q1 FY27. Labor code provisioning finalized at INR 14.4 Cr.
capex / expansion: INR 1,000 Cr committed for FY27. Adds ~1.1 lakh MT capacity (1.0 lakh MT piping, 10k MT material handling). Total installed capacity to reach ~1.35 Mn MT. Includes land acquisition for JNPT packaging unit.
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet; reinvestment into capacity expansion (5 new plants in last 12 months); focus on working capital to maintain high inventory levels (68% imported PVC) ensuring supply continuity.
risks & watch-items: Jal Jeevan/Nal Se Jal fund release delays (state-center coordination issues); PVC price volatility causing channel destocking; Geopolitical tensions impacting exports and feedstock; Unseasonal rainfall affecting agri demand.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; emphasizes volume growth over value due to price volatility; transparent about government spending delays; confident in market share gains despite industry contraction.
non-obvious takeaways: Industry volume contracted 9% in FY26 while Supreme grew 14%, implying massive market share shift from unorganized/smaller players; China's coal-based PVC production insulates domestic prices from Gulf crude volatility; Windows business margins expected to be superior to core piping due to customization.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

themes.title: PVC piping & building finishing
themes.need: Polymer-pipe and home-finishing plays are driven by agri/plumbing/real-estate finishing demand and PVC resin spreads - distinct from the value-added STEEL-tube structural/capex thesis.
themes.driver: Agri/plumbing/real-estate finishing demand and PVC resin-spread normalization.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Supreme Industries Limited manufactures a wide range of plastic products including uPVC/CPVC/HDPE/PVC piping systems, bath fittings and sanitaryware, roto-moulded tanks, moulded furniture, industrial components and material-handling products, flexible packaging and protective packaging films, composite LPG cylinders, and fabricated uPVC Windows & Doors. It serves the construction, packaging (FMCG/pharma/chemicals), automotive, furniture, consumer goods, and agriculture & irrigation industries across India and exports to 55 countries.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Fisheries crates business grew on favourable weather conditions supporting demand.
- Injection-molded dustbin business growth driven by proactive engagement across multiple sectors and a diverse bins portfolio.
- Dairy and fruit & vegetable crates business is constantly increasing across India.
- Composite LPG Cylinder demand supported by oil marketing companies (BPCL, IOCL, expected HPCL tender) and emerging biogas industry demand for CBG cylinders.
- Performance Films demand led by Dairy, Processed Foods, Edible Oil, Industrial applications and specialised lamination-grade films in the domestic market, with export volumes impacted by prevailing global conditions.
- Protective Packaging demand driven by infrastructure/construction-linked applications (Civil segment), expanding industrial and building usage (Insulation segment), and online/OEM/modern-retail traction (Consumer Products).
- Cross Laminated Film / tarpaulin demand expected to rebound sharply with the approaching peak season (April-May) and low inventory levels across the supply chain, after a cautious 'wait-and-watch' dealer approach caused by the U.S.-Iran conflict raising raw-material costs.
- Company expects newly signed Foreign Trade Agreements (FTAs) by the Government to make its products more price-competitive in international markets.
- Composite LPG Cylinder — BPCL: initial letter of intent for 2,00,000 nos. of 10 Kg LPG Cylinders successfully executed, followed by a repeat order of similar quantity under execution.
- Composite LPG Cylinder — IOCL: letter of intent for 2,31,035 nos. of LPG Cylinders under execution, albeit at a slower pace.
- Composite LPG Cylinder — HPCL expected to float a tender during the current year; Company expects to participate with a positive outcome.
- Performance Films Division anticipates continued momentum backed by order-pipeline buildup and ongoing capacity investments.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 margins supported by INR 70-80 Cr Q4 inventory gain; FY27 guidance 14-14.5% assumes normalized raw material costs. Current PVC prices dropped INR 34/kg in April, creating potential inventory loss headwinds for Q1 FY27. Labor code provisioning finalized at INR 14.4 Cr.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free balance sheet; reinvestment into capacity expansion (5 new plants in last 12 months); focus on working capital to maintain high inventory levels (68% imported PVC) ensuring supply continuity.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Protective Packaging Division carried out capacity expansion and technology upgradation across multiple plants during the year — an additional Capcell press at Malanpur; an upgraded XLPE line and a new high-productivity NBR line at Jadcherla; a new PU Foam Moulding plant at Hosur (a model the Company plans to replicate at other locations); two additional Capcell presses at Kharagpur; and a new EPE line at Urse. Further planned initiatives include relocating/upgrading an EPE line from Urse to Jadcherla, technical overhauling of EPE machines and installation of a new Calendar Roll at Hosur, overhauling of a Toshiba machine and installation of a Calendar Roll at Malanpur, and an XLPE line under evaluation at Kharagpur. The Division has completed land acquisition for a proposed greenfield manufacturing facility in the Western region close to a port, evaluating multiple product lines (PU Sheets, PU Moulding, XLPE, NBR, IXPE, Capcell, Litecell, PP Moulding) to serve export markets and West-zone customers. Separately, the Cross Laminated Film segment plans to launch a 'Cross Plastics' product in Q2 of the current year, subject to further refinement and successful customer trials. The Company funded large capital expenditure for capacity expansion — including the acquisition of 3 undertakings from the Wavin group on a slump-purchase basis — while remaining debt-free with a net cash surplus of ₹648.45 crores as on 31 March 2026, and continues to explore organic and inorganic growth avenues.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group] The Supreme Group comprises The Supreme Industries Ltd, Supreme Petrochem Ltd and Supreme Industries Overseas (FZE), a wholly owned UAE subsidiary — deck-level group figures should not be read as the listed entity alone.
- [Leadership] M. P. Taparia is Chairman & Managing Director; P C Somani is CFO; the management team is listed by vertical (e.g. A K Tripathi, Exe. VP Plastic Piping System; V L Malu, Exe. VP Industrial Components; Vivek Taparia, President Packaging).
- [Trade engagement] 5 regional Knowledge Centers impart technical education on plumbing best fitting practices and solvent welding, alongside plumber workshops and global trade fair participation.
